name: Question 3
problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)=⟨\,\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,t⟩.$
worked_solution:
Let $T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $r(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡(3t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(3t))+1} \\  & =\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\sqrt{(9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)^{2}+(-9\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\sqrt{{9}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡3t+{cos}^{2}⁡3t)} \\  & =\frac{9}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\,\frac{9}{\sqrt{10}}\,}{\sqrt{10}}=\frac{9}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Let T(t) denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter t. Since we are given the curve r(t) parametrized by the parameter t (not the arc length s), we will use the following formula for the curvature: κ(t)=‖T′(t)‖‖r′(t)‖

Now, we calculate r′(t) and find its magnitude:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(sin⁡3t),ddt(cos⁡3t),ddt(t)⟩=⟨3cos⁡3t,−3sin⁡3t,1⟩‖r′(t)‖=(3cos⁡3t)2+(−3sin⁡3t)2+(1)2=9(cos2⁡(3t)+sin2⁡(3t))+1=10

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=110⟨3cos⁡3t,−3sin⁡3t,1⟩.

Next, we calculate T′(t) and find its magnitude: T′(t)=110⟨ddt(3cos⁡3t),ddt(−3sin⁡3t),ddt(1)⟩=110⟨−9sin⁡3t,−9cos⁡3t,0⟩‖T′(t)‖=110(9sin⁡3t)2+(−9cos⁡t)2+02=11092(sin2⁡3t+cos2⁡3t)=910

Finally, the curvature is

κ(t)=‖T′(t)‖‖r′(t)‖=91010=910.
